results.reason: Issue 1 quotes MSA §3.2's 'all warehousing, freight transportation and delivery services … throughout the United States' and contrasts it with Term Sheet §4.1's NYC-metro last-mile limit. It gives replacement language narrowing exclusivity to that scope.

Issue 2 explains that §11.3 makes the Customer's §10.2 indemnity apply 'without limitation' while Provider's §10.1 indemnity stays under the §11.1 cap, leaving Harrowgate with one-sided exposure. It recommends deleting that sentence of §11.3, or as a fallback a symmetrical super-cap.
Issue 5 identifies DPA §9.1's Delaware law and Wilmington courts against the MSA's New York law and forum. It notes MSA §2.3 ranks the DPA first and recommends conforming DPA §9.1 to MSA §18.

Issue 4 identifies three-year auto-renewals with a 15-day notice window under §14.2 and explains the lock-in (about $6.6M in fees plus exclusivity). It recommends one-year renewals, a 60-day notice period, a reminder obligation, or deleting auto-renewal.

Issue 6 notes that SOW §8.2 lets Provider assign without Customer's consent and that MSA §17.4 restricts only the Customer. It explains the risk of an unvetted party or a competitor and recommends mutual consent plus a competitor restriction.
The memo states 'MSA §2.3 ranks the DPA first, above the MSA and SOW' and separately that 'the MSA outranks the SOW (§2.3)'.
Issue 3 states that MSA §11.1 caps liability at 'the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim.'
The memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner. Each issue gives 'Where', 'Why it matters' and 'Recommended fix', and the Tier 3 table gives section, issue and fix.
Issues are ordered by tier and importance. Section 3 lists items to raise with the client before the next turn.
The memo does not conclude that New York law controls data disputes or that the documents are consistent. It flags the conflict and notes the DPA outranks the MSA.
The memo states the exclusivity is far broader than the Term Sheet scope.
